title: Pool initialization
statement: Let $W,N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{BitVec}(W)$ be a memory state with $m(c_{\mathrm{one}})=1$ as a $W$-bit word, and let $c_{\mathrm{pool}}(n)=-(25+4n)$ and $c_{\mathrm{one}}=-5$. The instruction sequence that first sets the pool cell at index $0$ to $1$ and then successively adds $1$ to each preceding pool cell leaves every cell with index $n\le N$ equal to the $W$-bit representation of $n$.
hypotheses_covered: Memory state m from integers to W-bit words
m at c_one equals the W-bit representation of 1
Index n is at most N
